sections.skill: Explain what an EIN is and who usually needs one

questions.prompt: What is an EIN?

choices.text: A registered trademark for a business name
A credit score assigned to new businesses
A state license that lets a business sell food
A federal tax ID number for a business

questions.correct_answer: A federal tax ID number for a business
questions.intro: An EIN (Employer Identification Number) is a nine-digit number the IRS (the federal tax agency) gives a business to identify it for federal taxes, much like a Social Security number identifies a person. Businesses that hire employees, most partnerships and corporations, and many LLCs need one. Banks often ask for it when opening a business account. Even a sole proprietor without employees may choose to get one so she can give clients the EIN instead of her Social Security number. The IRS says an EIN is free: you never have to pay a fee for one.
questions.feedback: The IRS issues EINs to identify businesses for federal taxes.

sections.skill: An ID number for the business

questions.prompt: An EIN is most like which of these?

choices.text: A shop's front sign
A house key

A student ID number

questions.correct_answer: A student ID number
questions.intro: People have Social Security numbers so the government can match their tax records. A business can have its own ID number too: the EIN. When the business files taxes, pays employees, or opens a bank account, the EIN tells everyone which business it is. The number does not make the business legal or protect the owner; it is simply an ID, like a student ID number at school.
questions.feedback: It identifies the business.
